subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which is an example of a deforming process?
options: Vacuum forming a heated plastic sheet over a mould
questions.explain: Deforming changes a material's shape without removing or adding material, as when a heated plastic sheet is vacuum formed over a mould.

questions.q: Applying a finish such as varnish or paint to a product is done primarily to:
options: Protect the surface and improve appearance
questions.explain: Finishes protect a material from moisture, wear or corrosion and can enhance the product's appearance.

questions.q: A jig is used in manufacture to:
options: Measure the temperature of a kiln
Hold a workpiece and guide a tool for accuracy and repeatability
questions.explain: A jig holds the workpiece securely and guides the cutting tool, ensuring identical, accurate results across many parts.

questions.q: Quality control during production is mainly carried out to:
options: Check products meet the specification and catch faults early
Make the product more expensive on purpose
Increase the weight of every product
questions.explain: Quality control involves checks and tests throughout production to ensure products meet the specification and to identify defects.

questions.q: Injection moulding is most suited to which scale of production?
options: Mass or high-volume production of identical plastic parts
Making one bespoke piece of jewellery
questions.explain: Injection moulding has high tooling costs but very low per-unit costs, making it economical only for mass production of identical polymer parts.

questions.q: Laminating is a manufacturing technique that involves:
options: Bonding thin layers of material together, often to create a curved or strong shape
questions.explain: Laminating bonds thin layers (such as wood veneers) together, often around a former, to build up strength or create curved shapes.

questions.q: A CNC router is an example of:
options: CAM, where a computer controls the cutting machine
questions.explain: A CNC (computer numerical control) router is a CAM machine that cuts a workpiece automatically from a digital file.

questions.q: Continuous production differs from mass production because it:
options: Produces a different design every hour
Runs non-stop, often 24 hours a day, for products like chemicals or steel
Makes only one-off items by hand
questions.explain: Continuous production runs without interruption, around the clock, and is used for products that must be made in an uninterrupted flow.

questions.q: A template is most useful when you need to:
options: Mark out the same shape repeatedly and accurately
questions.explain: A template is a pattern used to mark out or cut identical shapes quickly and consistently.

questions.q: In manufacturing, a 'wastage' process is one that:
options: Heats a sheet and bends it
Cuts away or removes material to achieve the final shape
Adds material to build up a shape
questions.explain: Wastage processes such as sawing, drilling and milling remove unwanted material, leaving the desired shape behind.

questions.q: Which process is used to produce hollow plastic bottles?
questions.explain: Blow moulding inflates a heated tube of plastic against a mould to form hollow products such as bottles.

questions.q: A tolerance on a working drawing specifies:
options: The exact colour of the product
The permitted upper and lower limits a dimension may vary between
How long the product should last
questions.explain: A tolerance defines the acceptable maximum and minimum size limits for a dimension, ensuring parts fit together correctly.

questions.q: Which joining method gives a permanent fixing rather than a temporary one?
questions.explain: Welding fuses parts together permanently, whereas bolts, screws and press studs can be undone, making them temporary fixings.

questions.q: Soldering and brazing are both methods of:
options: Joining metals using a filler that melts at a lower temperature than the parts
Casting molten metal into a mould
questions.explain: Soldering and brazing join metal parts using a molten filler alloy that flows between them, without melting the base metals themselves.

questions.q: Annealing a metal before shaping it is done to:
options: Soften it so it is easier to bend and work
Make it harder and more brittle
questions.explain: Annealing heats and slowly cools a metal to relieve stresses and soften it, making it easier to form.

questions.q: Powder coating is a surface finish applied mainly to:
options: Metals, giving a tough durable coloured layer
questions.explain: Powder coating sprays charged powder onto metal which is then baked, forming a hard, durable, attractive finish.

questions.q: One-off (job) production is best suited to making:
options: A single bespoke item such as a tailored wedding dress
questions.explain: One-off production makes a single, often custom item to a unique specification, such as a made-to-measure product.

questions.q: Sand casting is a process in which:
options: Material is removed by a rotating cutter
Molten metal is poured into a sand mould and left to solidify
A sheet of plastic is bent over a former
questions.explain: In sand casting, molten metal is poured into a cavity formed in sand and allowed to cool and solidify into shape.

questions.q: Which process builds an object up layer by layer from a digital model?
questions.explain: 3D printing is an additive process that deposits material layer by layer to build a three-dimensional object directly from a CAD file.

questions.q: What does CAM stand for in design and technology?
questions.explain: CAM stands for Computer-Aided Manufacture, where computer-controlled machines such as CNC routers make a product from a CAD file.

questions.q: PVA and epoxy resin are both types of:
questions.explain: PVA and epoxy resin are adhesives used to bond materials, with epoxy being a strong two-part adhesive.

questions.q: Batch production is best defined as making:
options: A specified quantity of identical products in a group, then switching to another
A continuous non-stop flow of product 24 hours a day
questions.explain: Batch production makes a set number of identical items in one run, after which the equipment can be changed to produce a different batch.
